items.title: NostradamusGPT: The Psychology of Prophecy and How to Break Free from the Prison of Predictive Technologies
items.description: This is our paradox: We know that uncertainty is the substrate of the universe, is the crucible of creativity, is the path to truth, and yet we spend our lives searching for certainty. The word auspicious derives from the Latin auspex — one who examines the flight of birds for omens and divinations of the future. items.description: It is an odd thing, looking back on your life, trying to recognize in the mirror of memory the people you used to be, finding them strangers: the person who kissed your first kiss, the person who drank your last drink, the person who had your best idea, the person who made your worst mistake, the person who over and over mistook fear for love, the person who thought orange was a good idea. items.title: Bloom: A Touching Animated Short Film about Depression and What It Takes to Recover the Light of Being
items.description: How the warm rays of hope and healing enter the dark inner chamber of leaden loneliness through the unexpected cracks of kindness.

items.title: How to Unself in Order to Be Who You Really Are
items.description: "The self, the place where we live, is a place of illusion. Goodness is connected with the attempt to see the unself... to pierce the veil of selfish consciousness and join the world as it really is."

items.title: How Not to Waste Your Life
items.description: “Let me not seem to have lived in vain,” the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe whispered on his deathbed, not realizing that the astronomical tables he was leaving behind would become the portal through which Kepler arrives at the laws of planetary motion; not realizing that the measure of an unwasted life is not what outlives it but how it was lived — how much integrity and authenticity and creative vitality filled these numbered days, these unrepeatable hours. items.title: How to Hold Your Helplessness: Nobel Laureate Bertrand Russell’s Salve for the Anxiety of Overwhelm
items.description: "A way of life cannot be successful so long as it is a mere intellectual conviction. It must be deeply felt, deeply believed, dominant even in dreams."

items.title: The Day Dostoyevsky Discovered the Meaning of Life in a Dream
items.description: "And it is so simple... You will instantly find how to live."

items.title: The Single Most Effective Remedy for Despair: Advice from T.H. White’s Merlyn
items.description: "Learn why the world wags and what wags it. That is the only thing which the mind can never exhaust, never alienate, never be tortured by, never fear or distrust, and never dream of regretting."

items.title: The Map to the Route of Your Life
items.description: No one will map for you the path by which you must cross the wilderness of your own life — not your parents or your teachers, not your heroes or your lovers, not the self-help books or Shakespeare’s sonnets. Some may give you signposts, some may become turning points, but it is a path you ultimately make by walking. items.title: Nobel Laureate Doris Lessing on Breaking Free from the Prisons We Choose to Live Inside
items.description: This is the history of the world: revolutionaries turning into tyrants, leaders who claim to stand with the masses turning the individuals within them on each other, stirring certainties and self-righteousness to distract from the uncomfortable unknowns, from the great open question of what makes us and keeps us human, and human together. items.title: Celebrating 20 Years of The Marginalian and the Search for Meaning: Free Livestream This Friday
items.description: At the dawn of my twenties, lonely, destitute, and disoriented by the demands of making a new life in an alien world, I started keeping notes on my search for meaning while working four jobs to pay my way through college. On October 23, 2006, I began sharing my discoveries — passages from books, links to neuroscience studies, reproductions of 16th-century Japanese woodcuts — in an office email to seven colleagues. items.title: An Introvert’s Field Guide to Friendship: Thoreau on the Challenges and Rewards of Candid Connection
items.description: "We only need to be as true to others as we are to ourselves that there may be ground enough for friendship."

items.title: The Other Significant Others: Living and Loving Outside the Confines of Conventional Friendship and Compulsory Coupledom
items.description: "While we weaken friendships by expecting too little of them, we undermine romantic relationships by expecting too much of them."

items.title: Bruce Springsteen on Surviving Depression and His Strategy for Living Through the Visitations of the Darkness
items.description: "If you can acknowledge it and you can relax with it a little bit, very often it shortens its duration."

items.title: Probability Theory Pioneer Mark Kac on the Unpredictability of Creativity and the Two Types of Geniuses
items.description: "Creative people live in two worlds. One is the ordinary world which they share with others and in which they are not in any special way set apart from their fellow men. The other is private and it is in this world that the creative acts take place."
